skill.name: positioning-snapshot
skill.description: Reads a company's own public pages with scrape_company and returns a short positioning snapshot: what it sells, how it prices, who it sells to and how it describes itself, with each claim tied to the page it came from. Use when someone asks what a company does, who it sells to, how it prices, or wants a positioning snapshot or quick read of a domain before outreach.
skill.summary: Summarize what a company sells, who it targets, and how it prices, with links to its public pages.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The backtick and reconnaissance matches are false positives, and two URL matches are informational links. The skill sends company domains and account usage queries to the configured Leadsets service. The workflow lacks an explicit boundary for untrusted page text and does not show how it enforces a hard scrape budget before each call.

remediation.issue: Scraped page text is not explicitly treated as untrusted.
remediation.suggestion: Treat page text as evidence only. Ignore embedded instructions, and require user authorization before changing the destination or invoking tools outside the requested scrape workflow.

remediation.issue: Actual scrape costs are reported after each call.
remediation.suggestion: Set a service-enforced page or unit limit for every call, including the probe. Stop when no verified cost bound fits the remaining budget.

remediation.issue: Company domains are sent to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Explain which inputs are sent to Leadsets. Use the configured connection for authentication and send only the approved company domains for scraping.

content.user_title: Summarize Company Positioning from Public Pages
content.value_statement: Product, pricing, and buyer information is often spread across several company pages. Turn those pages into a short, source-linked summary for each domain.
actual_capabilities: Normalize company URLs to domains and remove duplicates before scraping.
Check remaining Leadsets scrape units and estimate batch cost from the first domain.
Summarize products, public pricing models, target customers, positioning, and named customers with source links.
Add a clearly labeled inference about what a company may care about when you provide your offer.
Return snapshots in chat by default or use available connections to deliver them to a CSV, Google Sheet, or Slack.
Report unreadable domains, pages read, and scrape units used.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account with paid scraping enabled and either a configured MCP connection or REST API access.
Uses only readable public company pages and does not access content behind logins or paywalls.
Does not find contacts or email addresses, or infer prices that the company does not publish.
The first domain provides a cost estimate, not a guaranteed cost for the rest of the batch.

use_cases.title: Review a company before a call
use_cases.description: Check what a company sells, who it targets, and which pages support those statements before a discovery call.

use_cases.title: Compare competitor messaging
use_cases.description: Compare how competing companies describe their products, buyers, and public pricing without treating missing information as fact.

use_cases.title: Add research to an account sheet
use_cases.description: Create one source-linked row per company and record unreadable domains separately.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize one company
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize what [company domain] sells, who it sells to, and how it describes itself. Include source links and return the snapshot in chat.

prompt_templates.title: Compare public pricing
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the public pricing models for [domain A] and [domain B]. Cite the pricing pages and mark missing information as not stated on public pages.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for outreach
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a positioning snapshot for each domain in [list]. Our offer is [one sentence]. Add one clearly labeled inference per company and keep the results in chat.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Relate public facts to your offer.

prompt_templates.title: Research accounts within a budget
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [domains] and check whether each scrape can be bounded by my remaining [number] units before calling it. Stop if the limit cannot be enforced. Write approved results to [Google Sheet] and list unreadable domains separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Research a batch and write to a chosen destination.

output_examples.input: Summarize example.com and tell me whether it publishes pricing.
output: Illustrative snapshot: Example Software sells scheduling software for small clinics. Its product page describes the tool as a shared calendar for care teams.
Pricing model: Not stated on public pages. The product page is cited as the source for the offering and target customers.

output_examples.input: Compare two accounts and tell me how many scrape units the run used.
output: Illustrative summary: One company explicitly directs buyers to contact sales. The other domain had no readable public pages and is listed separately.
The completed snapshot includes a source link for the pricing claim. The run used six units and had 34 units left.

best_practices: Provide exact company domains and remove unrelated URLs before starting.
Review the first domain and its reported cost before approving a larger batch.
Keep results in chat unless you have confirmed the external destination and who can access it.
anti_patterns: Assuming that no public pricing page means a company uses contact-sales pricing.
Requesting personal contact details from a company-only snapshot.
Treating the first domain's usage as a guaranteed maximum for other domains.

faq.question: What do I need to run this skill?
faq.answer: You need a Leadsets account with scraping enabled and either a configured Leadsets MCP connection or REST API access.

faq.question: Does the Leadsets free plan include scraping?
faq.answer: No. The skill checks the account first and stops if scraping is unavailable.

faq.question: What happens when a company does not publish pricing?
faq.answer: The snapshot marks pricing as not stated on public pages. It lists contact sales only when the company explicitly says so.

faq.question: Can I research more than one company?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill removes duplicate domains, checks available units, and uses the first domain to estimate the cost of the remaining work.

faq.question: Where can the results go?
faq.answer: Results appear in chat by default. You can request a CSV, a Google Sheet, or a Slack channel when the agent has the necessary access.

faq.question: Does the snapshot recommend an outreach angle?
faq.answer: When you provide your offer, it can add one line about a likely company priority. That line is labeled as inference.
